memory.title: Memory (injected into every AI analysis)
memory.fix_all: ✦ Correct names & terms in all meetings
memory.extract_title: Let the AI extract names / proper nouns from long-term memory and recent transcripts into the glossary
memory.compact_title: Rewrite long-term memory once: merge scattered entries, compress stale ones (the everyday incremental merge never does this)
memory.fix_hint: Correction uses the spellings in the glossary and memory and rewrites every transcript and report in the library (takes minutes).
memory.hint_content: Names, terms, company background, personal preferences. Maintained by hand; injected into every analysis and correction.
memory.hint_longterm: People, projects & clients, commitments & decisions, terms. Extracted and merged automatically (incrementally) after each transcript; you may edit.
memory.hint_glossary: Standard spelling of names and proper nouns: - Correct spelling (misheard: wrong1, wrong2) | note. Correct spellings are injected into the transcription prompt; the whole glossary is the authority for name / term correction.
memory.confirm_clear:
Clear {label}?
The previous content is backed up as .bak.md under memory/.
memory.confirm_clear_long: You can rebuild it afterwards with "coco memorize --all --force".
memory.fixall_confirm:
Correct names and proper nouns in the transcripts and reports of ALL meetings, using the glossary and memory?
Save the glossary first. Originals are backed up; each transcript can be restored with ↺ Restore original.
With many meetings this takes several minutes — keep the page open.
memory.extract_confirm_unsaved:
The glossary box has unsaved edits. Extraction works on the saved version and will refresh the box, so unsaved edits will be lost.
Save first? Continue anyway?
memory.extract_confirm:
Let the AI extract names / proper nouns from long-term memory and recent transcripts into the glossary?
The current glossary is backed up as glossary.bak.md.
memory.compact_confirm: Rewrite the whole long-term memory to merge and compress it? Takes a few minutes; the original is backed up as longterm.bak.md.

import.title: Import material
import.path_hint: Paste the full path of a file or folder. Audio / video is transcribed; txt / md / docx / pdf / srt / vtt / json … goes straight into the library. A folder imports every recognised file inside it.
import.path_tip_mac: In Finder, select the item and press Option+Cmd+C to copy its path.
import.path_tip_win: In Explorer, right-click the file → "Copy as path".
import.paste_hint: Paste a transcript, chat log, e-mail or someone else's minutes. SRT / VTT / JSON transcripts are detected and keep their timestamps. coco analyses it exactly like a local transcription and merges it into long-term memory.
import.title_placeholder: e.g. Chat with Alex about the roadmap
import.pasted: Imported; it will be merged into long-term memory

audiohelp.title: This computer cannot transcribe audio locally right now
audiohelp.body_windows: On Windows, local transcription relies on faster-whisper, and this computer has no working engine (without an NVIDIA GPU it is also very slow). Your recording is fine — it just needs to become text first.
audiohelp.body_mac: This Mac has no usable transcription engine (Apple Silicon needs mlx-whisper, Intel needs faster-whisper). Your recording is fine — it just needs to become text first.
audiohelp.body_linux: This computer has no usable transcription engine (faster-whisper is required). Your recording is fine — it just needs to become text first.
audiohelp.opt1_title: ① Transcribe with another tool, then drop the transcript here
audiohelp.opt1_body: Zoom, Teams, Google Meet, Otter, Fireflies, Tencent Meeting, Feishu Minutes and similar tools all export transcripts. txt, docx, pdf, srt, vtt, json and csv are accepted; timestamps are kept. Every analysis feature works the same.
audiohelp.opt2_body: If you already have the text, copy and paste is the fastest route.
audiohelp.opt3_title: ③ Install a transcription engine on this computer (advanced)
audiohelp.opt3_body: Run the command below in the coco folder, then restart coco. Without an NVIDIA GPU it runs on the CPU: a 45-minute recording can take 10–30 minutes.

caps.no_engine_toast: No transcription engine on this computer: audio cannot be transcribed, but transcripts (txt / docx / pdf / srt …) work with every analysis feature

caps.cpu_hint: Transcription runs on the CPU here (no NVIDIA GPU): a 45-minute recording can take 10–30 minutes. In a hurry, transcribe with another tool and import the text.

settings.title: ⚙ Settings
settings.output_source: Same as the material (whatever language the transcript is in)
settings.output_hint: The output language applies to reports, minutes, briefs, insights, pre-meeting briefs, chat answers, and the wording of long-term memory and the glossary. The transcription language is set separately in the top bar.
settings.ai_hint: By default coco uses the logged-in Claude Code CLI — no API key needed. You can also connect any Anthropic-compatible endpoint (e.g. DeepSeek's /anthropic) or OpenAI-compatible API (DeepSeek, OpenAI, a local Ollama). Send background work to a faster, cheaper channel without touching report quality.
settings.claude_missing: The claude command was not found on PATH. Install and log in to Claude Code (https://claude.com/claude-code), or switch the primary channel to an API type.
settings.profile_primary: Primary channel: reports / insights / pre-meeting briefs / chat
settings.profile_fast: Background channel: long-term memory / glossary / name correction
settings.fast_same: Background tasks use the same model as the primary channel
settings.api_key_placeholder: stored only in coco.config.json on this computer
settings.api_key_stored: stored (leave empty to keep; type to replace)
settings.tasks_hint: Which channel each kind of task uses. Suggested: deep analysis on the primary channel; long-term memory / glossary / name correction on the background channel.
settings.memory_delta: Incremental (recommended): the model outputs only new / changed entries and coco merges them by name — seconds
settings.memory_full: Full: the model rewrites the whole long-term memory every time (slow, and slower as memory grows)
settings.memory_hint: In incremental mode, run ⟲ Compact long-term memory under ◈ Memory from time to time for a full merge and compression pass.
